Resolve decision contract: post-Pluck outcome analysis.\n//!\n//! This module implements a structured decision system that runs after a Pluck\n//! operation completes. The resolver analyzes the agent's work and determines\n//! the appropriate next action, with strict validation and fail-safe defaults.\n//!\n//! ## Decision Flow\n//!\n//! 1. Agent completes Pluck (exit code 0 or non-zero)\n//! 2. Resolver receives agent output and context\n//! 3. Structured prompt is built from the resolve template\n//! 4. Agent must respond with valid JSON matching the schema\n//! 5. Parser validates the response exhaustively\n//! 6. Invalid/incomplete/unknown decisions fall back to safe defaults\n//!\n//! ## Decision Types\n//!\n//! - **Complete**: Task succeeded, bead should be closed\n//! - **Retry**: Temporary failure, release for immediate retry\n//! - **Blocked**: External dependency, cannot proceed without human input\n//! - **Split**: Task decomposes into multiple independent subtasks\n//!\n//! ## Safety Guarantees\n//!\n//! - Resolver NEVER implements changes or mutates beads\n//! - Invalid JSON → fallback to Retry (safe default)\n//! - Unknown decision type → fallback to Retry\n//! - Missing required fields → fallback to Retry\n//! - Timeout → fallback to Retry\n//!\n//! Depends on: `types`, `prompt`, `config`, `telemetry`.\n\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\nuse crate::prompt::PromptBuilder;\nuse crate::telemetry::Telemetry;\nuse crate::types::{Bead, BeadId};\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveDecision enum\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The four exhaustive resolve decision types.\n///\n/// Every possible post-Pluck outcome maps to exactly one of these decisions.\n/// No wildcards in matching — all variants must be explicitly handled.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ResolveDecision {\n    /// Task completed successfully — close the bead.\n    Complete {\n        /// Evidence that the task succeeded (git commits, tests passed, etc.)\n        evidence: String,\n        /// Human-readable summary of what was accomplished.\n        summary: String,\n    },\n\n    /// Temporary failure — release bead for immediate retry.\n    Retry {\n        /// Why the attempt failed (error message, diagnostic info).\n        reason: String,\n        /// Suggested retry strategy (same approach, different timeout, etc.).\n        strategy: RetryStrategy,\n    },\n\n    /// Blocked by external dependency — cannot proceed without human input.\n    Blocked {\n        /// What external resource is blocking progress (API, human decision, etc).\n        blocker: String,\n        /// What action is needed from a human (approve plan, provide credentials, etc).\n        required_action: String,\n        /// How critical this block is to project progress.\n        severity: BlockSeverity,\n    },\n\n    /// Task decomposes into multiple independent subtasks.\n    Split {\n        /// Proposed child beads (independent, sequentially completable).\n        children: Vec<ProposedChild>,\n        /// Rationale for why this decomposition is appropriate.\n        rationale: String,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl ResolveDecision {\n    /// Returns the decision type as a string for telemetry.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { .. } => \"complete\",\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { .. } => \"retry\",\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked { .. } => \"blocked\",\n            ResolveDecision::Split { .. } => \"split\",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate the decision has all required fields populated.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { evidence, summary } => {\n                if evidence.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Complete decision missing evidence\");\n                }\n                if summary.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Complete decision missing summary\");\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { reason, strategy } => {\n                if reason.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Retry decision missing reason\");\n                }\n                strategy.validate()?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked {\n                blocker,\n                required_action,\n                severity,\n            } => {\n                if blocker.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Blocked decision missing blocker\");\n                }\n                if required_action.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Blocked decision missing required_action\");\n                }\n                severity.validate()?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Split {\n                children,\n                rationale,\n            } => {\n                if children.is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision must have at least one child\");\n                }\n                if children.len() > 10 {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision cannot have more than 10 children\");\n                }\n                for (idx, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {\n                    child.validate(idx)?;\n                }\n                if rationale.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision missing rationale\");\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ResolveDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { summary, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Complete: {}\", summary)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { reason, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Retry: {}\", reason)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked {\n                blocker,\n                required_action,\n                ..\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"Blocked on {}: {}\", blocker, required_action)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Split { children, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Split into {} child tasks\", children.len())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RetryStrategy\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Strategy for retrying a failed attempt.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum RetryStrategy {\n    /// Same approach should work (transient failure, rate limit, etc).\n    Same,\n    /// Increase timeout for next attempt.\n    IncreaseTimeout,\n    /// Different approach needed (implementation incorrect, API changed, etc).\n    DifferentApproach,\n    /// Resource unavailable (service down, dependency missing, etc).\n    Backoff,\n}\n\nimpl RetryStrategy {\n    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // All variants are valid by construction\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            RetryStrategy::Same => \"same\",\n            RetryStrategy::IncreaseTimeout => \"increase_timeout\",\n            RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach => \"different_approach\",\n            RetryStrategy::Backoff => \"backoff\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BlockSeverity\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How critical a blocker is to project progress.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum BlockSeverity {\n    /// Cosmetic issue, nice-to-have enhancement, or low-priority cleanup.\n    Low,\n    /// Feature complete but blocked on polish, tests, or documentation.\n    Medium,\n    /// Critical blocker preventing core functionality or release.\n    High,\n}\n\nimpl BlockSeverity {\n    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // All variants are valid by construction\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            BlockSeverity::Low => \"low\",\n            BlockSeverity::Medium => \"medium\",\n            BlockSeverity::High => \"high\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ProposedChild\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A proposed child bead from a Split decision.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ProposedChild {\n    /// Short title for the child task.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Detailed description and acceptance criteria.\n    pub body: String,\n    /// Recommended priority (1-4, lower is higher priority).\n    pub priority: u8,\n}\n\nimpl ProposedChild {\n    fn validate(&self, idx: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.title.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"Child {} has empty title\", idx);\n        }\n        if self.body.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"Child {} ({}) has empty body\", idx, self.title);\n        }\n        if !(1..=4).contains(&self.priority) {\n            bail!(\n                \"Child {} ({}) has invalid priority {}, must be 1-4\",\n                idx,\n                self.title,\n                self.priority\n            );\n        }\n        if self.title.len() > 200 {\n            bail!(\n                \"Child {} title too long ({} chars, max 200)\",\n                idx,\n                self.title.len()\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveResponse\n// ──────────────────────────────────────��───────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The structured response schema for the resolve prompt.\n///\n/// Agents must respond with exactly this structure. All fields are required\n/// for the decision to be valid.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ResolveResponse {\n    /// The decision type (one of: complete, retry, blocked, split).\n    pub decision: ResolveDecision,\n}\n\nimpl ResolveResponse {\n    /// Parse and validate a JSON response string.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - JSON is malformed\n    /// - Structure doesn't match ResolveResponse\n    /// - Decision is invalid per validate()\n    pub fn parse_and_validate(json: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        // First, try to parse as JSON\n        let response: Self = serde_json::from_str(json)\n            .with_context(|| \"failed to parse resolve response as JSON\")?;\n\n        // Then validate the decision structure\n        response\n            .decision\n            .validate()\n            .with_context(|| \"parsed decision failed validation\")?;\n\n        Ok(response)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if the response JSON is valid without fully parsing.\n    ///\n    /// This is a cheap pre-check before attempting full parsing.\n    pub fn looks_valid(json: &str) -> bool {\n        // Quick heuristic checks\n        let json = json.trim();\n\n        // Must be non-empty and start with {\n        if json.is_empty() || !json.starts_with('{') {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Must contain a decision field\n        if !json.contains(\"\\\"decision\\\"\") {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Must contain one of the decision type markers\n        let has_decision_marker = json.contains(\"\\\"complete\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"retry\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"blocked\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"split\\\"\");\n\n        has_decision_marker\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveContext\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Context passed to the resolver for decision-making.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResolveContext<'a> {\n    /// The bead being resolved.\n    pub bead: &'a Bead,\n    /// Agent exit code from Pluck.\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    /// Agent stdout output.\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Agent stderr output.\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Duration of the Pluck operation.\n    pub duration: Duration,\n    /// Timestamp when Pluck started.\n    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    /// Whether the operation was interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM).\n    pub was_interrupted: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> ResolveContext<'a> {\n    /// Create a new resolve context.\n    pub fn new(\n        bead: &'a Bead,\n        exit_code: i32,\n        stdout: String,\n        stderr: String,\n        duration: Duration,\n        started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n        was_interrupted: bool,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            bead,\n            exit_code,\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration,\n            started_at,\n            was_interrupted,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format the duration for display in the prompt.\n    pub fn formatted_duration(&self) -> String {\n        let secs = self.duration.as_secs();\n        if secs >= 3600 {\n            format!(\"{}h {}m\", secs / 3600, (secs % 3600) / 60)\n        } else if secs >= 60 {\n            format!(\"{}m {}s\", secs / 60, secs % 60)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}s\", secs)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get a truncated version of stdout for the prompt (max 2000 chars).\n    pub fn truncated_stdout(&self) -> String {\n        self.stdout.chars().take(2000).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a truncated version of stderr for the prompt (max 2000 chars).\n    pub fn truncated_stderr(&self) -> String {\n        self.stderr.chars().take(2000).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// VerificationError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error type for binary identity verification failures.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VerificationError {\n    /// Binary identity verification failed.\n    VerificationFailed(String),\n    /// Verification not supported for this binary type.\n    NotSupported(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for VerificationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            VerificationError::VerificationFailed(msg) => {\n                write!(f, \"Verification failed: {}\", msg)\n            }\n            VerificationError::NotSupported(msg) => {\n                write!(f, \"Verification not supported: {}\", msg)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for VerificationError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Resolver\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The resolver analyzes Pluck outcomes and determines next actions.\npub struct Resolver {\n    /// Timeout for resolve agent calls (default 120s).\n    timeout: Duration,\n    /// Prompt builder for constructing the resolve prompt.\n    prompt_builder: PromptBuilder,\n    /// Telemetry client for emitting events.\n    telemetry: Option<Telemetry>,\n}\n\nimpl Resolver {\n    /// Create a new resolver with default timeout.\n    pub fn new(prompt_builder: PromptBuilder) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),\n            prompt_builder,\n            telemetry: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the timeout for resolve agent calls.\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {\n        self.timeout = timeout;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Set the telemetry client for event emission.\n    pub fn with_telemetry(mut self, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {\n        self.telemetry = Some(telemetry);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve a Pluck outcome into a structured decision.\n    ///\n    /// This method:\n    /// 1. Builds the resolve prompt with context\n    /// 2. Invokes an agent to analyze and decide\n    /// 3. Parses and validates the response\n    /// 4. Verifies binary identity after successful resolution\n    /// 5. Returns the decision or a safe fallback\n    ///\n    /// # Safety\n    ///\n    /// Any failure (timeout, invalid JSON, parse error, validation error, verification failure)\n    /// returns a safe fallback decision (Retry with generic reason) rather\n    /// than propagating the error. This ensures the worker can always continue.\n    pub async fn resolve(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> ResolveDecision {\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            exit_code = context.exit_code,\n            \"resolver: starting analysis\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the resolve prompt\n        let prompt = match self.build_prompt(context) {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"resolver: failed to build prompt, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"prompt_build_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // TODO: Actually invoke the agent here\n        // For now, return a fallback that indicates the system isn't fully wired yet\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            \"resolver: agent invocation not yet implemented, using fallback\"\n        );\n\n        let decision = self.fallback_decision(\"not_implemented\");\n\n        // Verify binary identity after successful resolution\n        if let Err(e) = self.verify_binary_identity(&decision) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"resolver: binary identity verification failed, using fallback\"\n            );\n            return ResolveDecision::Retry {\n                reason: format!(\"Binary identity verification failed: {}\", e),\n                strategy: RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach,\n            };\n        }\n\n        decision\n    }\n\n    /// Build the resolve prompt from context.\n    fn build_prompt(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> Result<String> {\n        let worker_id = \"resolver\"; // Resolver doesn't have a worker ID\n\n        let exit_status = if context.exit_code == 0 {\n            \"success\"\n        } else {\n            \"failure\"\n        };\n        let was_interrupted = if context.was_interrupted {\n            \"true\"\n        } else {\n            \"false\"\n        };\n\n        // Build the prompt with resolve-specific variables using the dedicated method\n        let built = self.prompt_builder.build_resolve(\n            context.bead,\n            &context.bead.workspace,\n            worker_id,\n            context.exit_code,\n            &context.formatted_duration(),\n            &context.truncated_stdout(),\n            &context.truncated_stderr(),\n            exit_status,\n            was_interrupted,\n        )?;\n\n        Ok(built.content)\n    }\n\n    /// Return a safe fallback decision.\n    ///\n    /// This is used when:\n    /// - Prompt building fails\n    /// - Agent invocation times out\n    /// - JSON parsing fails\n    /// - Decision validation fails\n    fn fallback_decision(&self, reason: &str) -> ResolveDecision {\n        ResolveDecision::Retry {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"Resolver error: {}. Safe fallback: retry with same approach.\",\n                reason\n            ),\n            strategy: RetryStrategy::Same,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify binary identity after successful resolution.\n    ///\n    /// This is a placeholder hook for binary identity verification.\n    /// Currently returns Ok(()) as a stub implementation.\n    ///\n    /// # Future Implementation\n    ///\n    /// This method should:\n    /// - Verify the binary matches expected checksums\n    /// - Validate binary signatures\n    /// - Check binary integrity\n    /// - Ensure the binary is from a trusted source\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(())` - Verification passed\n    /// - `Err(VerificationError)` - Verification failed\n    fn verify_binary_identity(&self, _decision: &ResolveDecision) -> Result<(), VerificationError> {\n        // Stub implementation - always passes for now\n        // TODO: Implement actual verification logic\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// Serialize};\n\nuse crate::prompt::PromptBuilder;\nuse crate::telemetry::Telemetry;\nuse crate::types::Bead;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveDecision enum\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The four exhaustive resolve decision types.\n///\n/// Every possible post-Pluck outcome maps to exactly one of these decisions.\n/// No wildcards in matching — all variants must be explicitly handled.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ResolveDecision {\n    /// Task completed successfully — close the bead.\n    Complete {\n        /// Evidence that the task succeeded (git commits, tests passed, etc.)\n        evidence: String,\n        /// Human-readable summary of what was accomplished.\n        summary: String,\n    },\n\n    /// Temporary failure — release bead for immediate retry.\n    Retry {\n        /// Why the attempt failed (error message, diagnostic info).\n        reason: String,\n        /// Suggested retry strategy (same approach, different timeout, etc.).\n        strategy: RetryStrategy,\n    },\n\n    /// Blocked by external dependency — cannot proceed without human input.\n    Blocked {\n        /// What external resource is blocking progress (API, human decision, etc).\n        blocker: String,\n        /// What action is needed from a human (approve plan, provide credentials, etc).\n        required_action: String,\n        /// How critical this block is to project progress.\n        severity: BlockSeverity,\n    },\n\n    /// Task decomposes into multiple independent subtasks.\n    Split {\n        /// Proposed child beads (independent, sequentially completable).\n        children: Vec<ProposedChild>,\n        /// Rationale for why this decomposition is appropriate.\n        rationale: String,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl ResolveDecision {\n    /// Returns the decision type as a string for telemetry.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { .. } => \"complete\",\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { .. } => \"retry\",\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked { .. } => \"blocked\",\n            ResolveDecision::Split { .. } => \"split\",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate the decision has all required fields populated.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { evidence, summary } => {\n                if evidence.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Complete decision missing evidence\");\n                }\n                if summary.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Complete decision missing summary\");\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { reason, strategy } => {\n                if reason.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Retry decision missing reason\");\n                }\n                strategy.validate()?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked {\n                blocker,\n                required_action,\n                severity,\n            } => {\n                if blocker.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Blocked decision missing blocker\");\n                }\n                if required_action.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Blocked decision missing required_action\");\n                }\n                severity.validate()?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Split {\n                children,\n                rationale,\n            } => {\n                if children.is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision must have at least one child\");\n                }\n                if children.len() > 10 {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision cannot have more than 10 children\");\n                }\n                for (idx, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {\n                    child.validate(idx)?;\n                }\n                if rationale.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision missing rationale\");\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ResolveDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { summary, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Complete: {}\", summary)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { reason, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Retry: {}\", reason)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked {\n                blocker,\n                required_action,\n                ..\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"Blocked on {}: {}\", blocker, required_action)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Split { children, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Split into {} child tasks\", children.len())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RetryStrategy\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Strategy for retrying a failed attempt.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum RetryStrategy {\n    /// Same approach should work (transient failure, rate limit, etc).\n    Same,\n    /// Increase timeout for next attempt.\n    IncreaseTimeout,\n    /// Different approach needed (implementation incorrect, API changed, etc).\n    DifferentApproach,\n    /// Resource unavailable (service down, dependency missing, etc).\n    Backoff,\n}\n\nimpl RetryStrategy {\n    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // All variants are valid by construction\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            RetryStrategy::Same => \"same\",\n            RetryStrategy::IncreaseTimeout => \"increase_timeout\",\n            RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach => \"different_approach\",\n            RetryStrategy::Backoff => \"backoff\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BlockSeverity\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How critical a blocker is to project progress.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum BlockSeverity {\n    /// Cosmetic issue, nice-to-have enhancement, or low-priority cleanup.\n    Low,\n    /// Feature complete but blocked on polish, tests, or documentation.\n    Medium,\n    /// Critical blocker preventing core functionality or release.\n    High,\n}\n\nimpl BlockSeverity {\n    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // All variants are valid by construction\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            BlockSeverity::Low => \"low\",\n            BlockSeverity::Medium => \"medium\",\n            BlockSeverity::High => \"high\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ProposedChild\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A proposed child bead from a Split decision.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ProposedChild {\n    /// Short title for the child task.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Detailed description and acceptance criteria.\n    pub body: String,\n    /// Recommended priority (1-4, lower is higher priority).\n    pub priority: u8,\n}\n\nimpl ProposedChild {\n    fn validate(&self, idx: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.title.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"Child {} has empty title\", idx);\n        }\n        if self.body.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"Child {} ({}) has empty body\", idx, self.title);\n        }\n        if !(1..=4).contains(&self.priority) {\n            bail!(\n                \"Child {} ({}) has invalid priority {}, must be 1-4\",\n                idx,\n                self.title,\n                self.priority\n            );\n        }\n        if self.title.len() > 200 {\n            bail!(\n                \"Child {} title too long ({} chars, max 200)\",\n                idx,\n                self.title.len()\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveResponse\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The structured response schema for the resolve prompt.\n///\n/// Agents must respond with exactly this structure. All fields are required\n/// for the decision to be valid.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ResolveResponse {\n    /// The decision type (one of: complete, retry, blocked, split).\n    pub decision: ResolveDecision,\n}\n\nimpl ResolveResponse {\n    /// Parse and validate a JSON response string.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - JSON is malformed\n    /// - Structure doesn't match ResolveResponse\n    /// - Decision is invalid per validate()\n    pub fn parse_and_validate(json: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        // First, try to parse as JSON\n        let response: Self = serde_json::from_str(json)\n            .with_context(|| \"failed to parse resolve response as JSON\")?;\n\n        // Then validate the decision structure\n        response\n            .decision\n            .validate()\n            .with_context(|| \"parsed decision failed validation\")?;\n\n        Ok(response)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if the response JSON is valid without fully parsing.\n    ///\n    /// This is a cheap pre-check before attempting full parsing.\n    pub fn looks_valid(json: &str) -> bool {\n        // Quick heuristic checks\n        let json = json.trim();\n\n        // Must be non-empty and start with {\n        if json.is_empty() || !json.starts_with('{') {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Must contain a decision field\n        if !json.contains(\"\\\"decision\\\"\") {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Must contain one of the decision type markers\n        let has_decision_marker = json.contains(\"\\\"complete\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"retry\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"blocked\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"split\\\"\");\n\n        has_decision_marker\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveContext\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Context passed to the resolver for decision-making.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResolveContext<'a> {\n    /// The bead being resolved.\n    pub bead: &'a Bead,\n    /// Agent exit code from Pluck.\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    /// Agent stdout output.\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Agent stderr output.\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Duration of the Pluck operation.\n    pub duration: Duration,\n    /// Timestamp when Pluck started.\n    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    /// Whether the operation was interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM).\n    pub was_interrupted: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> ResolveContext<'a> {\n    /// Create a new resolve context.\n    pub fn new(\n        bead: &'a Bead,\n        exit_code: i32,\n        stdout: String,\n        stderr: String,\n        duration: Duration,\n        started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n        was_interrupted: bool,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            bead,\n            exit_code,\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration,\n            started_at,\n            was_interrupted,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format the duration for display in the prompt.\n    pub fn formatted_duration(&self) -> String {\n        let secs = self.duration.as_secs();\n        if secs >= 3600 {\n            format!(\"{}h {}m\", secs / 3600, (secs % 3600) / 60)\n        } else if secs >= 60 {\n            format!(\"{}m {}s\", secs / 60, secs % 60)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}s\", secs)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get a truncated version of stdout for the prompt (max 2000 chars).\n    pub fn truncated_stdout(&self) -> String {\n        self.stdout.chars().take(2000).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a truncated version of stderr for the prompt (max 2000 chars).\n    pub fn truncated_stderr(&self) -> String {\n        self.stderr.chars().take(2000).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// VerificationError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error type for binary identity verification failures.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VerificationError {\n    /// Binary identity verification failed.\n    VerificationFailed(String),\n    /// Verification not supported for this binary type.\n    NotSupported(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for VerificationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            VerificationError::VerificationFailed(msg) => {\n                write!(f, \"Verification failed: {}\", msg)\n            }\n            VerificationError::NotSupported(msg) => {\n                write!(f, \"Verification not supported: {}\", msg)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for VerificationError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Resolver\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The resolver analyzes Pluck outcomes and determines next actions.\npub struct Resolver {\n    /// Timeout for resolve agent calls (default 120s).\n    timeout: Duration,\n    /// Prompt builder for constructing the resolve prompt.\n    prompt_builder: PromptBuilder,\n    /// Telemetry client for emitting events.\n    telemetry: Option<Telemetry>,\n}\n\nimpl Resolver {\n    /// Create a new resolver with default timeout.\n    pub fn new(prompt_builder: PromptBuilder) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),\n            prompt_builder,\n            telemetry: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the timeout for resolve agent calls.\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {\n        self.timeout = timeout;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Set the telemetry client for event emission.\n    pub fn with_telemetry(mut self, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {\n        self.telemetry = Some(telemetry);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve a Pluck outcome into a structured decision.\n    ///\n    /// This method:\n    /// 1. Builds the resolve prompt with context\n    /// 2. Invokes an agent to analyze and decide\n    /// 3. Parses and validates the response\n    /// 4. Verifies binary identity after successful resolution\n    /// 5. Returns the decision or a safe fallback\n    ///\n    /// # Safety\n    ///\n    /// Any failure (timeout, invalid JSON, parse error, validation error, verification failure)\n    /// returns a safe fallback decision (Retry with generic reason) rather\n    /// than propagating the error. This ensures the worker can always continue.\n    pub async fn resolve(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> ResolveDecision {\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            exit_code = context.exit_code,\n            \"resolver: starting analysis\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the resolve prompt\n        let prompt = match self.build_prompt(context) {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"resolver: failed to build prompt, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"prompt_build_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // TODO: Actually invoke the agent here\n        // For now, return a fallback that indicates the system isn't fully wired yet\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            \"resolver: agent invocation not yet implemented, using fallback\"\n        );\n\n        let decision = self.fallback_decision(\"not_implemented\");\n\n        // Verify binary identity after successful resolution\n        if let Err(e) = self.verify_binary_identity(&decision) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"resolver: binary identity verification failed, using fallback\"\n            );\n            return ResolveDecision::Retry {\n                reason: format!(\"Binary identity verification failed: {}\", e),\n                strategy: RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach,\n            };\n        }\n\n        decision\n    }\n\n    /// Build the resolve prompt from context.\n    fn build_prompt(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> Result<String> {\n        let worker_id = \"resolver\"; // Resolver doesn't have a worker ID\n\n        let exit_status = if context.exit_code == 0 {\n            \"success\"\n        } else {\n            \"failure\"\n        };\n        let was_interrupted = if context.was_interrupted {\n            \"true\"\n        } else {\n            \"false\"\n        };\n\n        // Build the prompt with resolve-specific variables using the dedicated method\n        let built = self.prompt_builder.build_resolve(\n            context.bead,\n            &context.bead.workspace,\n            worker_id,\n            context.exit_code,\n            &context.formatted_duration(),\n            &context.truncated_stdout(),\n            &context.truncated_stderr(),\n            exit_status,\n            was_interrupted,\n        )?;\n\n        Ok(built.content)\n    }\n\n    /// Return a safe fallback decision.\n    ///\n    /// This is used when:\n    /// - Prompt building fails\n    /// - Agent invocation times out\n    /// - JSON parsing fails\n    /// - Decision validation fails\n    fn fallback_decision(&self, reason: &str) -> ResolveDecision {\n        ResolveDecision::Retry {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"Resolver error: {}. Safe fallback: retry with same approach.\",\n                reason\n            ),\n            strategy: RetryStrategy::Same,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify binary identity after successful resolution.\n    ///\n    /// This is a placeholder hook for binary identity verification.\n    /// Currently returns Ok(()) as a stub implementation.\n    ///\n    /// # Future Implementation\n    ///\n    /// This method should:\n    /// - Verify the binary matches expected checksums\n    /// - Validate binary signatures\n    /// - Check binary integrity\n    /// - Ensure the binary is from a trusted source\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(())` - Verification passed\n    /// - `Err(VerificationError)` - Verification failed\n    fn verify_binary_identity(&self, _decision: &ResolveDecision) -> Result<(), VerificationError> {\n        // Stub implementation - always passes for now\n        // TODO: Implement actual verification logic\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// Safe fallback: retry with same approach.\",\n                reason\n            ),\n            strategy: RetryStrategy::Same,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify binary identity after successful ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Resolver\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The resolver analyzes Pluck outcomes and determines next actions.\npub struct Resolver {\n    /// Timeout for resolve agent calls (default 120s).\n    timeout: Duration,\n    /// Prompt builder for constructing the resolve prompt.\n    prompt_builder: PromptBuilder,\n    /// Telemetry client for emitting events.\n    telemetry: Option<Telemetry>,\n}\n\nimpl Resolver {\n    /// Create a new resolver with default timeout.\n    pub fn new(prompt_builder: PromptBuilder) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),\n            prompt_builder,\n            telemetry: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the timeout for resolve agent calls.\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {\n        self.timeout = timeout;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Set the telemetry client for event emission.\n    pub fn with_telemetry(mut self, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {\n        self.telemetry = Some(telemetry);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve a Pluck outcome into a structured decision.\n    ///\n    /// This method:\n    /// 1. Builds the resolve prompt with context\n    /// 2. Invokes an agent to analyze and decide\n    /// 3. Parses and validates the response\n    /// 4. Verifies binary identity after successful resolution\n    /// 5. Returns the decision or a safe fallback\n    ///\n    /// # Safety\n    ///\n    /// Any failure (timeout, invalid JSON, parse error, validation error, verification failure)\n    /// returns a safe fallback decision (Retry with generic reason) rather\n    /// than propagating the error. This ensures the worker can always continue.\n    pub async fn resolve(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> ResolveDecision {\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            exit_code = context.exit_code,\n            \"resolver: starting analysis\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the resolve prompt\n        let _prompt = match self.build_prompt(context) {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"resolver: failed to build prompt, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"prompt_build_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // TODO: Actually invoke the agent here\n        // For now, return a fallback that indicates the system isn't fully wired yet\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            \"resolver: agent invocation not yet implemented, using fallback\"\n        );\n\n        let decision = self.fallback_decision(\"not_implemented\");\n\n        // Verify binary identity after successful resolution\n        if let Err(e) = self.verify_binary_identity(&decision) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"resolver: binary identity verification failed, using fallback\"\n            );\n            return ResolveDecision::Retry {\n                reason: format!(\"Binary identity verification failed: {}\", e),\n                strategy: RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach,\n            };\n        }\n\n        decision\n    }\n\n    /// Build the resolve prompt from context.\n    fn build_prompt(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> Result<String> {\n        let worker_id = \"resolver\"; // Resolver doesn't have a worker ID\n\n        let exit_status = if context.exit_code == 0 {\n            \"success\"\n        } else {\n            \"failure\"\n        };\n        let was_interrupted = if context.was_interrupted {\n            \"true\"\n        } else {\n            \"false\"\n        };\n\n        // Build the prompt with resolve-specific variables using the dedicated method\n        let built = self.prompt_builder.build_resolve(\n            context.bead,\n            &context.bead.workspace,\n            worker_id,\n            context.exit_code,\n            &context.formatted_duration(),\n            &context.truncated_stdout(),\n            &context.truncated_stderr(),\n            exit_status,\n            was_interrupted,\n        )?;\n\n        Ok(built.content)\n    }\n\n    /// Return a safe fallback decision.\n    ///\n    /// This is used when:\n    /// - Prompt building fails\n    /// - Agent invocation times out\n    /// - JSON parsing fails\n    /// - Decision validation fails\n    fn fallback_decision(&self, reason: &str) -> ResolveDecision {\n        ResolveDecision::Retry {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"Resolver error: {}. Safe fallback: retry with same approach.\",\n                reason\n            ),\n            strategy: RetryStrategy::Same,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify binary identity after successful resolution.\n    ///\n    /// This is a placeholder hook for binary identity verification.\n    /// Currently returns Ok(()) as a stub implementation.\n    ///\n    /// # Future Implementation\n    ///\n    /// This method should:\n    /// - Verify the binary matches expected checksums\n    /// - Validate binary signatures\n    /// - Check binary integrity\n    /// - Ensure the binary is from a trusted source\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(())` - Verification passed\n    /// - `Err(VerificationError)` - Verification failed\n    fn verify_binary_identity(&self, _decision: &ResolveDecision) -> Result<(), VerificationError> {\n        // Stub implementation - always passes for now\n        // TODO: Implement actual verification logic\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n//         duration,\n            started_at,\n            was_interrupted,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format the duration for display in the prompt.\n    pub fn formatted_duration(&self) -> String {\n        let secs = self.duration.as_secs();\n        if secs >= 3600 {\n            format!(\"{}h {}m\", secs / 3600, (secs % 3600) / 60)\n        } else if secs >= 60 {\n            format!(\"{}m Eq)]\npub enum VerificationError {\n    /// Binary identity verification failed.\n    VerificationFailed(String),\n    /// Verification not supported for this binary type.\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Resolver\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The resolver      }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the timeout for resolve agent calls.\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {\n        self.timeout = timeout;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Set the telemetry client for event emission.\n    pub fn with_telemetry(mut self, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {\n        self.telemetry = Some(telemetry);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve a Pluck outcome into a structured decision.\n    ///\n    /// This method:\n    /// 1. Builds the resolve prompt with context\n    /// 2. Invokes an agent to analyze and decide\n    /// 3. Parses and validates the response\n    /// 4. Verifies binary identity after successful resolution\n    /// 5. Returns the decision or a safe fallback\n    ///\n    /// # Safety\n    ///\n    /// Any failure (timeout, invalid JSON, parse error, validation error, verification failure)\n    /// returns a safe fallback decision (Retry with generic reason) rather\n    /// than propagating the error. This ensures the worker can always continue.\n    pub async fn resolve(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> ResolveDecision {\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            exit_code = context.exit_code,\n            \"resolver: starting analysis\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the resolve prompt\n        let _prompt = match self.build_prompt(context) {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"resolver: failed to build prompt, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"prompt_build_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // TODO: Actually invoke the agent here\n        // For now, return a fallback that indicates the system isn't fully wired yet\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            \"resolver: agent invocation not yet implemented, using fallback\"\n        );\n\n        let decision = self.fallback_decision(\"not_implemented\");\n\n        // Verify binary identity after successful resolution\n        if let Err(e) = self.verify_binary_identity(&decision) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"resolver: binary identity verification failed, using fallback\"\n            );\n            return ResolveDecision::Retry {\n                reason: format!(\"Binary identity verification failed: {}\", e),\n                strategy: RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach,\n            };\n        }\n\n        decision\n    }\n\n    /// Build the resolve prompt from context.\n    fn build_prompt(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> Result<String> {\n        let worker_id = \"resolver\"; // Resolver doesn't have a worker ID\n\n        let exit_status = if context.exit_code == 0 {\n            \"success\"\n        } else {\n            \"failure\"\n        };\n        let was_interrupted = if context.was_interrupted {\n            \"true\"\n        } else {\n            \"false\"\n        };\n\n        // Build the prompt with resolve-specific variables using the dedicated method\n        let built = self.prompt_builder.build_resolve(\n            context.bead,\n            &context.bead.workspace,\n            worker_id,\n            context.exit_code,\n            &context.formatted_duration(),\n            &context.truncated_stdout(),\n            &context.truncated_stderr(),\n            exit_status,\n            was_interrupted,\n        )?;\n\n        Ok(built.content)\n    }\n\n    /// Return a safe fallback decision.\n    ///\n    /// This is used when:\n    /// - Prompt building fails\n    /// - Agent invocation times out\n    /// - JSON parsing fails\n    /// - Decision validation fails\n    fn fallback_decision(&self, reason: &str) -> ResolveDecision {\n        ResolveDecision::Retry {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"Resolver error: {}. Safe fallback: retry with same approach.\",\n                reason\n            ),\n            strategy: RetryStrategy::Same,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify binary identity after successful resolution.\n    ///\n    /// This is a placeholder hook for binary identity verification.\n    /// Currently returns Ok(()) as a stub implementation.\n    ///\n    /// # Future Implementation\n    ///\n    /// This method should:\n    /// - Verify the binary matches expected checksums\n    /// - Validate binary signatures\n    /// - Check binary integrity\n    /// - Ensure the binary is from a trusted source\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(())` - Verification passed\n    /// - `Err(VerificationError)` - Verification failed\n    fn verify_binary_identity(&self, _decision: &ResolveDecision) -> Result<(), VerificationError> {\n        // Stub implementation - always passes for now\n        // TODO: Implement actual verification logic\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// exhaustion_with_idle_action_wait_survives_sleep() {\n    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};\n\n    /// Mock store that returns NoWork initially, then a bead after N calls.\n    struct DelayedBeadStore {\n        call_count: AtomicU32,\n        bead_after: u32,\n        bead: Mutex<Option<Bead>>,\n        /// Tracks claimed beads (moved here from `bead` on claim).\n        claimed: DelayedBeadStore {\n        async fn ready(&self, _filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n            // After the bead is released, signal the worker to exit by returning an error.\n            if self.bead_released.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == 1 {\n                return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"test complete - bead was released\"));\n            }\n            let count = self.call_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            if count >= self.bead_after {\n                // Return the bead if it's available (not yet claimed or claimed but not yet released).\n                let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n                let claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n                if bead.is_some() && !claimed.iter().any(|b| b.id == bead.as_ref().unwrap().id) {\n                    Ok(vec![bead.clone().unwrap()])\n                } else {\n                    Ok(vec![])\n                }\n            } else {\n                Ok(Vec::new())\n            }\n        }\n\n        async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n            let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n            let claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            let mut all: Vec<Bead> = claimed.clone();\n            if let Some(b) = bead.as_ref() {\n                if !all.iter().any(|x| x.id == b.id) {\n                    all.push(b.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(all)\n        }\n\n        async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead> {\n            let claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            if let Some(b) = claimed.iter().find(|b| b.id == *id) {\n                return Ok(b.clone());\n            }\n            let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n            match bead.as_ref() {\n                Some(b) if b.id == *id => Ok(b.clone()),\n                _ => anyhow::bail!(\"bead not found: {id}\"),\n            }\n        }\n\n        async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n            let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n            let mut claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            match bead.as_ref() {\n                Some(b) if b.id == *id => {\n                    let mut cloned = b.clone();\n                    cloned.status = BeadStatus::InProgress;\n                    cloned.assignee = Some(actor.to_string());\n                    claimed.push(cloned.clone());\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(cloned))\n                }\n                _ => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                    reason: \"no bead\".to_string(),\n                }),\n            }\n        }\n\n        async fn claim_auto(&self, _actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n\n        async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n            // Remove the bead from claimed after it's been processed.\n            let mut claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            claimed.retain(|b| b.id != *id);\n            // Mark that the bead has been released - worker should exit on next cycle.\n            self.bead_released.store(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            Ok(())\n        }\n\n        async fn block(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n\n        async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()> {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n\n make_bead(\"needle-sort-b\", 1);\n            b.created_at = now - chrono::Duration::hours(2);\n            b\n        },\n        {\n            let mut b = make_bead(\"needle-sort-d\", 2);\n            b.created_at = now;\n            b\n        },\n    ];\n\n    // Create two independent stores with the same beads (shuffled).\n    let store1: Arc<dyn BeadStore> =        reversed\n    }));\n\n    let pluck = PluckStrand::new(vec![], Telemetry::new(\"test-worker\".to_string()));\n\n    // Evaluate both — should return the same top candidate.\n    let result1 =    needle::types::StrandResult::BeadFound(beads) => beads.first().map(|b| b.id.clone()),\n        _ => None,\n    };\n    let id2 = match result2 {\n        needle::types::StrandResult::BeadFound(beads) => beads.first().map(|b| b.id.clone()),\n        _ => None,\n    };\n\n    assert_eq!(\n        id1, id2,\n        \"deterministic ordering: same beads   \"P1 bead created earliest should be selected first\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[tokio::test]\nasync fn deterministic_ordering_tiebreak_by_id() {\n    // When priority and creation time are identical, bead ID 256,\n        1000,\n        i32::MAX,\n    ];\n\n    for code in test_codes {\n        // Should not panic.\n        let outcome = Outcome::classify(code, false);\n        // Verify specific mappings.\n        match code {\n            0 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Success),\n            1 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Failure),\n            124 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Timeout),\n            127 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::AgentNotFound),\n            c if c > 128 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Crash(c)),\n            c if c < 0 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Crash(c)),\n            _ => {} // Other codes just shouldn't panic\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Verify interrupted flag always wins.\n    for code in [-1, 0, 1, 127, 137] {\n        assert_eq!(\n            Outcome::classify(code, true),\n            Outcome::Interrupted,\n            \"was_interrupted=true must always return Interrupted for code {code}\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// Test 7: Worker config validation at boot\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n/// Test that worker rejects invalid config at boot.\n///\n/// This test builds a Worker in-process with intentionally invalid config.\n/// The Explore strand MUST be isolated to prevent scanning real user directories.\n///\n/// REQUIRED ISOLATION — see \"Test Isolation Policy\" in CLAUDE.md and ADR-006.\n///\n/// Why isolation is required for in-process Worker tests:\n/// - Workers built in-process never go through a child process, so setting\n///   `HOME` in a Command::new() call has no effect (no child process worker_boot_rejects_invalid_config() {\n    let store: Arc<dyn BeadStore> = Arc::new(IntegrationMockStore::empty());\n    let _home_guard = HomeGuard::isolate();\n    let mut config = test's tempdir to prevent scanning real user directories\n    config.strands.explore.workspace_root = _home_guard._temp_dir.path().to_path_buf();\n    config.strands.explore.workspaces = Vec::new();\n\n    let mut worker = Worker::new(config, \"test-worker\".to_string(), store);\n    let result = worker.run().await;\n\n    assert!(\n        result.is_err(),\n        \"worker should        .arg(\"init\")\n        .current_dir(&workspace)\n        .output();\n\n    // bead init may fail if the workspace is already initialized - that's OK for this test\n    if let Ok(init_output) = initialized\"\n            if !stderr.contains(\"already\") && !stderr.contains(\"exists\") {\n                panic!(\"bead init failed: {}\", stderr);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // stderr_output.contains(\"possible causes\")\n            || stderr_output.contains(\"Reasons\")\n            || stderr_output.contains(\"reasons\"),\n        \"error message should include a 'Common stderr_output.contains(\"•\") ||   // Unicode bullets\n        stderr_output.contains(\"*\") ||   // Asterisk bullets\n        stderr_output.contains(\"1.\") ||  // Numbered lists\n        stderr_output.contains(\"\\n\\n\"), // At minimum, multi-paragraph structure\n        \"error message should be structured with bullets or multiple paragraphs for readability. \\\n         Got stderr:\\n{}\",\n        stderr_output\n    );\n\n    // ASSERTION 8: Error message must indicate the problem occurred at startup\n    // This prevents users from thinking it's a runtime issue\n    assert!(\n        stderr_output.contains(\"startup\")\n            || stderr_output.contains(\"Startup\")\n            || stderr_output.contains(\"boot\")\n            || stderr_output.contains(\"initialization\")\n            || stderr_output.contains(\"aborting\"),\n        \"error message should indicate the problem occurred at startup/boot time. \\\n         Got stderr_output.contains(\"invalid configuration\") ||\n        stderr_output.contains(\"aborting to prevent\"),\n        \"error message should explain why startup is aborting (to prevent claiming When the inner process is `None`, methods return\n/// sensible defaults for testing scenarios.\npub struct MockProcess {\n    inner: Option<std::process::Child>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for MockProcess {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl MockProcess {\n    /// Create a new MockProcess with no inner child process.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        MockProcess { inner: /// Kill the mock process.\n    ///\n    /// If an inner child process exists, delegates to its `kill()` method.\n    /// Otherwise, returns Ok(()) as a no-op for testing.\n    pub fn kill(&mut self)  return;\n    }\n\n    println!(\"✓ SIGTERM sent\");\n\n    // Wait for the worker to exit (should be within a few seconds)\n    let shutdown_timeout = Duration::from_secs(10);\n    let shutdown_start              return;\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    println!(\"✓ Worker exited with status: {:?}\", exit_status);\n\n    // Verify the heartbeat file was cleaned up\n    let cleanup_check_start = Instant::now();\n    let cleanup_timeout = Duration::from_secs(2);\n\n    // Give a small buffer for the file system to sync\n    while cleanup_check_start.elapsed() < cleanup_timeout {\n        if !heartbeat_file.exists() {\n            println!(\n                \"✓ Heartbeat file cleaned up after {:?}\",\n                cleanup_check_start.elapsed()\n test failed\");\n    }\n\n    // Verify total test execution time is within 60 seconds\n    let total_time = start.elapsed();\n    println!(\"✓ Total test execution time: {:?}\", total_time);\n\n    assert!(\n        total_time < Duration::from_secs(60),\n        \"test should complete within 60 seconds, took {:?}\",\n        total_time\n    );\n\n    println!(\"✓ Integration test passed: heartbeat cleanup on signal\");\n}\n\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// Integration tests: worker_binary_path override (bf-63dmk)\n// exit.\n///\n/// This test validates the graceful shutdown workflow when a worker completes\n/// its work naturally (no signals, just normal exhaustion).\n///\n/// Test strategy:\n/// 1. Spawn a real needle worker subprocess with limited work\n/// 2. Wait for the worker to create its heartbeat file\n/// 3. Wait for the worker to complete work and exit naturally\n/// 4. Verify the heartbeat file is cleaned up after exit\n/// 5. Verify no stale heartbeat files remain\n#[test]\nfn heartbeat_cleanup_on_normal_exit_integration() {\n    use std::path::PathBuf;\n    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n\n    // Find the needle binary\n    let needle_binary = std::env::current_exe()\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|p| {\n            let path_str = p.to_string_lossy().to_string();\n            if path_str.contains(\"integration_tests\") {\n                Some(\n                    p.parent()\n                        .map(|grandparent| {\n                            let needle_path = grandparent.join(\"needle\");\n                            if needle_path.exists() {\n                                needle_path\n                            } else {\n                                let debug_path = grandparent.join(\"debug\").join(\"needle\");\n                                if debug_path.exists() {\n                                    debug_path\n                                } else {\n                                    grandparent.join(\"release\").join(\"needle\")\n                                }\n                            }\n                        })\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(\"needle\")),\n                )\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(\"needle\"));\n\n    if !needle_binary.exists() {\n        println!(\n            \"Skipping test: needle binary not found at {}\",\n            needle_binary.display()\n        );\n        return;\n    }\n\n    println!(\"Using needle binary: {}\", needle_binary.display());\n\n    // Create a temporary workspace with a bead that will complete quickly\n    let temp_dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create temp dir\");\n    let workspace = temp_dir.path().join(\"workspace\");\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&workspace).expect(\"failed to create workspace\");\n\n    let beads_dir = workspace.join(\".beads\");\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&beads_dir).expect(\"failed to create beads dir\");\n\n    // Create a simple bead that will succeed exhaustion_with_idle_action_wait_survives_sleep() {\n    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};\n\n    /// Mock store that returns NoWork initially, then a bead after N calls.\n    struct DelayedBeadStore {\n        call_count: AtomicU32,\n        bead_after: u32,\n        bead: Mutex<Option<Bead>>,\n        /// Tracks claimed beads (moved here from `bead` on claim).\n        claimed: Mutex<Vec<Bead>>,\n        /// Signals that the bead has been released and the worker should exit.\n        bead_released: AtomicU32,\n    }\n\n    #[async_trait]\n    impl BeadStore for DelayedBeadStore {\n        async fn ready(&self, _filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n            // After the bead is released, signal the worker to exit by returning an error.\n            if self.bead_released.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == 1 {\n                return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"test complete - bead was released\"));\n            }\n            let count = self.call_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            if count >= self.bead_after {\n                // Return the bead if it's available (not yet claimed or claimed but not yet released).\n                let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n                let claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n                if bead.is_some() && !claimed.iter().any(|b| b.id == bead.as_ref().unwrap().id) {\n                    Ok(vec![bead.clone().unwrap()])\n                } else {\n                    Ok(vec![])\n                }\n            } else {\n                Ok(Vec::new())\n            }\n        }\n\n        async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n            let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n            let claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            let mut all: Vec<Bead> = claimed.clone();\n            if let Some(b) = bead.as_ref() {\n                if !all.iter().any(|x| x.id == b.id) {\n                    all.push(b.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(all)\n        }\n\n        async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead> {\n            let claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            if let Some(b) = claimed.iter().find(|b| b.id == *id) {\n                return Ok(b.clone());\n            }\n            let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n            match bead.as_ref() {\n                Some(b) if b.id == *id => Ok(b.clone()),\n                _ => anyhow::bail!(\"bead not found: {id}\"),\n            }\n        }\n\n        async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n            let bead = self.bead.lock().unwrap();\n            let mut claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n            match bead.as_ref() {\n                Some(b) if b.id == *id => {\n                    let mut cloned = b.clone();\n                    cloned.status = BeadStatus::InProgress;\n                    cloned.assignee = Some(actor.to_string());\n                    claimed.push(cloned.clone());\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(cloned))\n                }\n                _ => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                    reason: \"no bead\".to_string(),\n                }),\n            }\n        }\n\n        async fn claim_auto(&self, _actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n\n        async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n            // Remove the bead from claimed after it's been processed.\n            let mut claimed = self.claimed.lock().unwrap();\n ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n#[tokio::test]\nasync fn deterministic_ordering_same_beads_same_order() {\n    // Given the same set of beads with varied priorities and creation times,\n    // two independent sorts should produce identical ordering.\n    use needle::strand::PluckStrand;\n    use needle::strand::Strand;\n\n    let now = Utc::now();\n\n    let beads = vec![\n        {\n            let mut b = make_bead(\"needle-sort-c\", 3);\n            b.created_at = now - chrono::Duration::hours(1);\n            b\n        },\n        {\n            let mut b = make_bead(\"needle-sort-a\", 1);\n            b.created_at = now - chrono::Duration::hours(3);\n            b\n        },\n        {\n            let mut b = make_bead(\"needle-sort-b\", 1);\n            b.created_at = now - chrono::Duration::hours(2);\n            b\n        },\n        {\n            let mut b = make_bead(\"needle-sort-d\", 2);\n            b.created_at = now;\n            b\n        },\n    ];\n\n    // Create two independent stores with the same beads (shuffled).\n    let store1: Arc<dyn BeadStore> = Arc::new(IntegrationMockStore::new(beads.clone()));\n    let store2: Arc<dyn BeadStore> = Arc::new(IntegrationMockStore::new({\n        let mut reversed = beads.clone();\n        reversed.reverse();\n        reversed\n    }));\n\n    let pluck = PluckStrand::new(vec![], Telemetry::new(\"test-worker\".to_string()));\n\n    // Evaluate both — should return the same top candidate.\n    let result1 = pluck.evaluate(store1.as_ref(), &HashSet::new()).await;\n    let result2 = pluck.evaluate(store2.as_ref(), &HashSet::new()).await;\n\n    // Extract candidate IDs.\n    let id1 = match result1 {\n        needle::types::StrandResult::BeadFound(beads) => beads.first().map(|b| b.id.clone()),\n        _ => None,\n    };\n    let id2 = match result2 {\n        needle::types::StrandResult::BeadFound(beads) => beads.first().map(|b| b.id.clone()),\n        _ => None,\n    };\n\n    assert_eq!(\n        id1, id2,\n        \"deterministic ordering: same beads must produce same top candidate\"\n    );\n\n    // The top candidate should be the highest-priority, oldest bead.\n    assert_eq!(\n        id1,\n        Some(BeadId::from(\"needle-sort-a\")),\n        \"P1 bead created earliest should be selected first\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[tokio::test]\nasync fn deterministic_ordering_tiebreak_by_id() {\n    // When priority and creation time are identical, bead ID ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// Test 6: Outcome classification exhaustiveness\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n#[test]\nfn outcome_classify_covers_all_exit_code_ranges() {\n    // Verify that classify handles the full i32 range without panicking.\n    // This is a smoke test to ensure no gaps exist.\n    let test_codes: Vec<i32> = vec![\n        i32::MIN,\n        -1000,\n        -1,\n        0,\n        1,\n        2,\n        50,\n        99,\n        100,\n        123,\n        124,\n        125,\n        126,\n        127,\n        128,\n        129,\n        130,\n        137,\n        143,\n        255,\n        256,\n        1000,\n        i32::MAX,\n    ];\n\n    for code in test_codes {\n        // Should not panic.\n        let outcome = Outcome::classify(code, false);\n        // Verify specific mappings.\n        match code {\n            0 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Success),\n            1 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Failure),\n            124 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Timeout),\n            127 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::AgentNotFound),\n            c if c > 128 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Crash(c)),\n            c if c < 0 => assert_eq!(outcome, Outcome::Crash(c)),\n            _ => {} // Other codes just shouldn't panic\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Verify interrupted flag always wins.\n    for code in [-1, 0, 1, 127, 137] {\n        assert_eq!(\n            Outcome::classify(code, true),\n            Outcome::Interrupted,\n            \"was_interrupted=true must always return Interrupted for code {code}\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// Test 7: Worker config validation at boot\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n/// Test that worker rejects invalid config at boot.\n///\n/// This test builds a Worker in-process with intentionally worker_binary_path_tilde_expansion_trailing_slashes() {\n    use needle::util::expand_tilde;\n    use std::env;\n    use std::fs;\n\n    // Create a completely isolated temp directory for this test\n    let temp_dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create temp dir\");\n    let isolated_home = temp_dir.path().join(\"fake-home\");\n    fs::create_dir_all(&isolated_home).expect(\"failed to assert_eq!(\n        expanded, expected_nested_with_slash,\n        \"~/some/nested/path/ should expand with trailing slash preserved\"\n    );\n\n    // Test 4: Multiple trailing slashes are passed\");\n    println!(\"  Isolated home: {}\", isolated_home.display());\n    println!(\"  Bare tilde ~ -> {}\", isolated_home.display());\n    println!(\"  ~/ -> {}\", isolated_home.display());\n    println!(\"  ~/bin/ -> {}\", bin_dir.display());\n    println!(\"  ~/bin/// -> {}\", bin_dir.display());\n}\n\n/// Test tilde expansion with parent directory edge cases.\n///\n/// This test shutdown workflow (bf-4sbb)\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n/// Integration test that verifies heartbeat cleanup happens on normal worker exit.\n///\n/// This test validates the graceful shutdown workflow when a worker completes\n/// its work naturally (no signals, just normal exhaustion).\n///\n/// Test strategy:\n/// 1. Spawn a real needle worker subprocess with limited work\n/// 2. Wait for the worker to create its heartbeat file\n/// 3. Wait for the worker to complete work and exit naturally\n/// 4. Verify no stale heartbeat files remain\n#[test]\nfn heartbeat_cleanup_on_normal_exit_integration() {\n    use std::path::PathBuf;\n    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n\n    // Find the needle binary\n    let needle_binary = std::env::current_exe()\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|p| {\n            let path_str = p.to_string_lossy().to_string();\n            if path_str.contains(\"integration_tests\") {\n                Some(\n                    p.parent()\n                        .map(|grandparent| {\n                            let needle_path = grandparent.join(\"needle\");\n                            if needle_path.exists() {\n                                needle_path\n                            } else {\n                                let debug_path = grandparent.join(\"debug\").join(\"needle\");\n                                if debug_path.exists() {\n                                    debug_path\n                                } else {\n                                    grandparent.join(\"release\").join(\"needle\")\n                                }\n                            }\n                        })\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(\"needle\")),\n                )\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(\"needle\"));\n\n    if !needle_binary.exists() {\n        println!(\n            \"Skipping test: needle binary not found at {}\",\n            needle_binary.display()\n        );\n worker_pid);\n\n    // ProcessGuard ensures cleanup if test panics\n    let mut child_guard = ProcessGuard::new(child, Some(worker_pid));\n\n    // Give the worker time to start up and create its println!(\"Waiting for heartbeat file: {}\", heartbeat_file.display());\n\n    let start = Instant::now();\n    let heartbeat_timeout = Duration::from_secs(30);\n    let poll_interval = Duration::from_millis(200);\n    let mut heartbeat_found = false;\n\n    // Wait up to 30 seconds for the heartbeat file to appear with proper timeout handling\n    while start.elapsed() < heartbeat_timeout {\n        if heartbeat_file.exists() {\n            heartbeat_found = true;\n            println!(\"✓ Heartbeat file created after {:?}\", start.elapsed());\n            break;\n        }\n        std::thread::sleep(poll_interval);\n    }\n\n    // Explicit timeout check with clear error message\n    if !heartbeat_found {\n        panic!(\n            \"Heartbeat file not found cleanup_check_start.elapsed()\n            );\n            break;\n        }\n        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n    }\n\n    if heartbeat_file.exists() {\n        panic!(\"Heartbeat file was not cleaned up after normal exit, test failed\");\n    }\n\n    // Verify no stale heartbeat files remain in the heartbeat directory\n    if heartbeat_dir.exists() {\n total_time < Duration::from_secs(60),\n        \"test should complete within 60 seconds, took {:?}\",\n        total_time\n    );\n}\n\n/// Integration test that verifies heartbeat cleanup happens on
